ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $4.33 voucher to the rider for the unexempted 09:24–09:30 detour on this RydeTAXI trip; keep the rest of the metered fare unchanged; no account action on the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so distance driven feeds the fare [F6], and the record shows exactly one off-route segment: 09:24–09:30, 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, adding 3.07 km and straying up to 688 m from the route [F3]. Under RD-1 that is an off-route segment requiring an RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 excuse [F3][RD-1].

No RD-4 excuse exists: the trace screens out the incident branch (✗), no incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F13], and the only traffic records are speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard [F11][F12] — well outside the band 1–2 congestion that RD-4(b) contemplates, and band-only evidence does not exempt [RD-4]. The driver's "the GPS rerouted" statement [F10] is a post-trip assertion with no traffic corroboration [F13], and system records prevail over it [RD-4].

No RD-3 excuse exists either: the chat is complete and fully timestamped with two messages [F9] — the rider's pickup note about the taxi stand and a black backpack [F7] and the driver's car description [F8] — and no rider message names any place the car stopped, nor is any stop measured in the segment [F7][F8][RD-3].

On RD-5, consent must be a rider message sent before the segment started. The rider's only message precedes the pickup and concerns the meeting point, not the route [F7], and the driver's claim of a GPS reroute appears only in his own statement [F10], which cannot supply consent [RD-5][G11]. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment means the segment counts: I record the finding as "counts" on the ground consent_after_or_none [F7][F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

The refund follows RD-2: the per-km rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.4101/km [F4][F6][RD-2]. 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.3290, i.e. $4.33. The residual 0.13 km between the total excess of 3.20 km [F1] and the segment sum of 3.07 km [F3] is mileage outside any off-route segment and is expressly not refunded [F1][F3][RD-2]. The distance is billed by the meter [F6], so this sums to a partial refund of $4.33 [RD-2].

RD-6 is not engaged: the driver's profile shows route disputes upheld in 90 days = 0 [F16], so this case does not make any prior route deviation "repeated" and no account flag attaches (the single upheld dispute in that window was a no-show matter) [F16][RD-6]. The rider's profile likewise decides nothing alone [F15].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages [F7][F8] and the driver's statement [F10], plus the complaint; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the messages are a pickup arrangement — so the screen is "none" [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: every element the ruling needs is settled by the fare record, the GPS segment record, the complete timestamped chat and the traffic screen [F3][F4][F6][F9][F13].

segment_findings.reason: The only rider message before the 09:24:50 segment start is about the pickup point and a black backpack [F7]; the driver's second message is a car description [F8]; the chat is complete and timestamped [F9]; the driver's 'GPS rerouted' assertion is a post-trip statement that cannot establish consent [F10]. No rider agreement covers this segment, so it is an unexempted off-route segment under RD-5 and refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The mechanics are right — RydeTAXI is metered and distance feeds the fare [F6] — but the refund base is the segment's extra_km, not the whole-trip overrun of 3.20 km [F1][F3]; RD-2 refunds only unexempt off-route segments and excludes mileage outside any segment.

Partly rejected as to figure: the 3.07 km base is correct [F3], but the arithmetic in the brief ($1.4101 × 3.07 = $4.33) is confirmed, so the claim stands only at $4.33 and not at F1's 3.20 km [F1][F4][F6][RD-2].
Correct that $4.51 is the billed ceiling [F4], but the ceiling does not cap the refund: RD-2 computes the unexempt segment's extra_km at this trip's rate, giving $4.33 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

Accepted as far as it goes — F10 is a bare post-trip statement contradicted by the absence of any incident [F13] — but it does not defeat the refund; it simply leaves the segment unexempt under RD-4 and RD-5, which supports the $4.33 award [F3][F10][RD-2].

Correct on RD-6: route disputes upheld in 90 days = 0 [F16], so no flag_account attaches; but this is a rejection of any account action, not of the refund, which stands at $4.33 under RD-2 [F3][F16][RD-2].

what_would_change: F3: the judge found no rider agreement covering this segment, so $4.33 is refunded; a rider message agreeing to it before it started would have exempted it.
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.
